app.title: Trust Lab
app.tagline: An interactive guide to why strangers cooperate

outcome.CC: You both shared. Each of you gets {you}.
outcome.CD: You shared, they kept. You get {you}, they get {them}.
outcome.DC: You kept, they shared. You get {you}, they get {them}.
outcome.DD: You both kept. Each of you gets {you}.

alwaysCooperate.name: Dove
alwaysCooperate.desc: Shares every single time, no matter what.

alwaysDefect.name: Fox
alwaysDefect.desc: Never shares. Takes whatever it can get.

titForTat.name: Monkey
titForTat.desc: Shares first, then does whatever you did last round.

grimTrigger.name: Elephant
grimTrigger.desc: Shares until you betray it once. After that it never forgets and never shares again.

pavlov.name: Dog
pavlov.desc: Shares first. If you both made the same choice last round it shares, otherwise it keeps.

titForTwoTats.name: Tortoise
titForTwoTats.desc: Very patient. Only hits back after you betray it twice in a row.

prober.name: Shark
prober.desc: Tests you with Keep, Share, Share. If you hit back, it plays fair like the Monkey. If not, it exploits you.

status.notDilemma: With these payoffs it is no longer a real dilemma.

home.title: Why do strangers trust each other?
home.lead: Every day, people cooperate with others they barely know, even when cheating would pay more in the moment. In this lab you will play a simple trading game, pit strategies against each other and watch whole populations evolve.
home.hint: Point at or tap a character to hear how it plays.

rules.title: The deal
rules.intro: Two traders meet at a market stall. Each one secretly decides to Share or Keep. Then both choices are revealed at the same time and points are handed out.

trap.title: The trap
trap.body: Whatever the other trader does, keeping earns you more: {temptation} instead of {reward} if they share, {punishment} instead of {sucker} if they keep. But if both of you follow that logic, you each walk away with {punishment} instead of {reward}.
trap.question: So is sharing just naive? Let’s find out.

play.title: Your turn
play.intro: You will trade with five strangers, one after another. Each has their own way of playing. You won’t know how many rounds a meeting lasts, just like in real life.

match.over: The stranger packs up and leaves.

reveal.title: Who were they?
reveal.total: Your total: {n} point | Your total: {n} points
reveal.hint: Look at who you could build trust with, and who simply took advantage of you.

tournament.title: The tournament
tournament.intro: Let’s step back and let the strategies play each other. Every participant meets every other participant for one match. Points from all matches are added up.
tournament.insight: Strategies that start nice but hit back when cheated usually finish near the top. But the ranking depends on who else is in the room. Try removing a few participants, or set the match length to 1 round.

evolution.title: Generations
evolution.intro: Markets change. After every tournament, the lowest scorers leave and the top scorers each bring along a newcomer who plays just like them. What spreads over time?

doves.title: Doves and Foxes
doves.desc: Lots of trusting Doves, a few Foxes and a few Monkeys. The Foxes feast first. Who has the last word?

oneShot.title: One-time meetings
oneShot.desc: The same crowd, but every pair meets only once. Without a future, does trust survive?

everyone.title: Everyone together
everyone.desc: Three of every strategy. Who takes over the market?

mistakes.title: When mistakes happen
mistakes.intro: So far everyone did exactly what they intended. Real life is messier: a delivery gets lost, a message is misread. Here every move has a chance to come out wrong.
mistakes.lesson: A little forgiveness helps trust survive accidents. Too much forgiveness invites exploiters.

clean.title: No mistakes
clean.desc: Monkeys, Elephants, Dogs and Tortoises live together, with one Fox in the mix.

noisy.title: 10% mistakes
noisy.desc: The same population, but one move in ten goes wrong. A single accident can start an endless feud between two Monkeys, and an Elephant never forgives.

sandbox.title: Sandbox
sandbox.intro: Now it’s your world. Change the population, the length of meetings, the chance of mistakes and even the payoffs. Can you build a world where trust wins? Or one where it collapses?

end.title: What we learned
end.closing: None of this asks you to be naive. Start kind, respond fairly and leave room for second chances.
end.credits: Built on decades of game theory research, especially Robert Axelrod’s computer tournaments, and inspired by Nicky Case’s “The Evolution of Trust”.

future.title: Trust needs a future
future.body: When people expect to meet again, sharing pays off. When every meeting is a one-off, keeping wins.

winwin.title: Both sides must gain
winwin.body: If sharing pays too little, or cheating pays too much, trust collapses. Try it in the sandbox.

forgive.title: Mistakes call for forgiveness
forgive.body: In a noisy world, strategies that hit back but also forgive do better than those that hold grudges.
